issues.title: isMinimal mode sets h1 to illegible text-[8px] size
issues.description: When isMinimal=true, the h1 title gets `text-[8px] sm:text-[8px]` which renders at 8px on all screens. This is almost certainly a unit/implementation error — likely intended to be `text-base` or `text-sm` for minimal mode, not 8px which is unreadable.
issues.impact: Renders article title illegibly when isMinimal mode is active (used by WikiReference peek view). Users see an 8px title that's impossible to read.
issues.suggestion: Replace `text-[8px] sm:text-[8px]` with appropriate minimal sizing like `text-sm sm:text-base` or similar.

issues.title: dangerouslySetInnerHTML with raw SVG output — potential XSS vector
issues.description: Mermaid renders SVG output using `dangerouslySetInnerHTML` without sanitization. If the chart string contains user-controlled or untrusted content, this creates an XSS vulnerability.
issues.impact: Security risk — malicious chart content could execute scripts in the article context.
issues.suggestion: Sanitize SVG output with DOMPurify before injecting, or use the mermaid.run() pattern which inserts SVG as DOM elements rather than innerHTML.

issues.title: Two parallel MDX component maps risk behavioral drift
issues.description: WikiArticle.tsx defines WIKI_COMPONENTS (64+ entries) while mdx-components-shared.ts defines baseMdxComponents (48+ entries) with overlapping but not identical sets. Changes to one may not be reflected in the other, especially for new block components.
issues.impact: New blocks may render via one path but not the other, causing inconsistent rendering between wiki article pages and other MDX contexts.
issues.suggestion: Unify into a single source of truth. Either export components from a shared config, or have one map reference the other with overrides.

issues.title: Error state uses hard page reload instead of soft retry
issues.description: The 'Try Refreshing' button calls `window.location.reload()` which performs a full hard navigation, losing all state. There's no mechanism to retry the MDX compilation.
issues.impact: Poor UX — users lose their scroll position, any input state, and context. Full page reload is jarring.
issues.suggestion: Expose a retry callback from WikiArticle that attempts to re-compile the MDX, or use router.refresh() for a soft re-render.

issues.title: No keyboard arrow navigation between tabs
issues.description: Tab buttons can be focused but the component does not handle Left/Right/Up/Down arrow keys for navigating between tabs. ARIA tabs pattern requires arrow key navigation.
issues.impact: Keyboard-only users cannot efficiently navigate between tabs. Violates WAI-ARIA tabs pattern.
issues.suggestion: Implement onKeyDown handler for ArrowLeft/ArrowRight (horizontal) navigation between tab buttons, with proper roving tabindex.

issues.title: Missing aria-orientation on tablist
issues.description: The tablist element has no `aria-orientation` attribute. Screen readers need this to understand the navigation direction.
issues.impact: Screen reader users may not know tabs are arranged horizontally.
issues.suggestion: Add `aria-orientation="horizontal"` to the tablist div.

issues.title: Rendered Mermaid SVG has no accessible description
issues.description: The SVG diagram has no aria-label, role="img", or title element. Screen readers cannot describe the diagram content to users.
issues.impact: Visually impaired users have no access to diagram content.
issues.suggestion: Add role="img" with an aria-label describing the diagram, or include a hidden text summary alongside the SVG.

issues.title: Modal dialog missing focus trap
issues.description: The full-screen modal does not trap keyboard focus. Users can Tab outside the modal into background content.
issues.impact: Keyboard users can lose context and focus background elements, violating modal dialog accessibility requirements.
issues.suggestion: Implement a focus trap that cycles Tab within the modal content, and shift-Tab from the first to last focusable element.

issues.title: No Escape key handler to skip the gate or close summary
issues.description: The pre-question gate modal does not handle the Escape key to dismiss or skip. Users must click 'Skip to article' explicitly.
issues.impact: Keyboard users cannot quickly dismiss the modal. Standard modal behavior expects Escape to close.
issues.suggestion: Add an onKeyDown handler for Escape that triggers the skip/close behavior.

issues.title: Focus trap only monitors focusin, doesn't cycle Tab within dialog
issues.description: The focus trap resets focus to the close button if focus leaves the dialog, but it does not cycle Tab between the first and last focusable elements within the dialog.
issues.impact: Once focus reaches the last focusable element, pressing Tab again exits to the browser chrome rather than wrapping to the first element.
issues.suggestion: Implement a proper focus trap that detects when focus reaches the last tabbable element and wraps to the first.

issues.title: Gated timer uses setInterval instead of setTimeout chain
issues.description: The 2-second gated delay uses setInterval(50ms) for countdown. This is an anti-pattern — interval callbacks can pile up if the render is blocked.
issues.impact: Timer may drift or accumulate if the main thread is busy. Minor but unnecessary pattern risk.
issues.suggestion: Use a single setTimeout with the total delay, or use requestAnimationFrame-based timing for smoother countdown.

issues.title: Custom popover missing Escape key handler
issues.description: The custom createPortal-based popover does not handle Escape key to close. Keyboard users cannot dismiss it.
issues.impact: Keyboard-only users are trapped in the popover once opened.
issues.suggestion: Add an onKeyDown on the popover div that calls setIsOpen(false) on Escape.

issues.title: Custom popover missing Escape key handler
issues.description: Same issue as WikiRelatedPopover — the custom popover does not handle Escape key to close.
issues.impact: Keyboard-only users are trapped in the popover once opened.
issues.suggestion: Add an onKeyDown handler for Escape on the popover div.

issues.title: Sidebar resize only supports mouse, no keyboard or touch
issues.description: The drag-to-resize feature uses mousedown/mousemove/mouseup events only. No keyboard or touch support is implemented.
issues.impact: Users relying on keyboard or touch devices cannot resize the sidebar.
issues.suggestion: Add touch event handlers and keyboard support (e.g., Arrow keys when resize handle is focused).

issues.title: Returns null before mount causing layout flash
issues.description: The component returns `null` before hydration (when `mounted` is false). This causes the sidebar to flash from missing to visible on every page load.
issues.impact: Layout shift on page load — poor user experience and Core Web Vitals impact.
issues.suggestion: Use SSR-safe default width and apply localStorage value after mount without returning null.

issues.title: No screen-reader-accessible formula description
issues.description: Formula visualization uses styled divs and spans. There is no aria-label, aria-describedby, or off-screen text that screen readers can use to understand the formula.
issues.impact: Visually impaired users cannot access formula content.
issues.suggestion: Add an aria-label to the formula container with a text description of the formula, or include an off-screen text representation.

issues.title: MCQ options use buttons instead of radio group pattern
issues.description: Options are rendered as individual `<button>` elements rather than `<input type="radio">` within a `radiogroup` role. This reduces screen reader efficiency.
issues.impact: Screen reader users cannot navigate options as a group or quickly hear the selected state.
issues.suggestion: Either add role="radiogroup" with proper radio input elements, or add role="radio" and aria-checked to the buttons.

issues.title: Error state missing aria-live for screen reader announcement
issues.description: The error UI has no `aria-live` region. Screen readers won't automatically announce that the article failed to render.
issues.impact: Screen reader users may not know the article failed to load unless they navigate to the error area.
issues.suggestion: Add `role="alert"` or `aria-live="assertive"` to the error container.

issues.title: Warning type uses unicode emoji without accessible label
issues.description: The 'warning' type render uses `⚠ Warning` text with an emoji. The emoji may not be announced by screen readers and could render inconsistently across platforms.
issues.impact: Minor accessibility gap — warning emphasis may be missed.
issues.suggestion: Add `role="img" aria-label="Warning"` to the emoji span, or use an SVG icon with proper aria-label.

issues.title: Content shell skeleton has no aria-busy or aria-live
issues.description: When navigation is pending and the skeleton is shown, there's no `aria-busy="true"` on the container or `aria-live="polite"` to announce the transition.
issues.impact: Screen reader users may not detect that content is loading.
issues.suggestion: Add `aria-busy={isPending}` to the main container.

issues.title: Sidebar skeleton has no aria-busy indicator
issues.description: The sidebar loading skeleton has no `aria-busy="true"` to indicate content is loading.
issues.impact: Screen reader users may not know the sidebar is still loading.
issues.suggestion: Add `aria-busy="true"` to the aside element.

issues.title: Right sidebar skeleton has no aria-busy indicator
issues.description: Same issue as WikiSidebarSkeleton — no `aria-busy` for loading state.
issues.impact: Screen reader users may not know the sidebar is loading.
issues.suggestion: Add `aria-busy="true"` to the skeleton container.

issues.title: Banner missing role="alert" for screen reader attention
issues.description: The wrong-answer context banner should use `role="alert"` so screen readers announce it when the article loads.
issues.impact: Users arriving from a wrong answer may not realize why the banner context appears.
issues.suggestion: Add `role="alert"` to the banner div.

issues.title: Tooltip uses HTML title attribute not accessible on touch
issues.description: The tooltip showing the old value uses the HTML `title` attribute, which is not accessible on touch devices and has poor screen reader support.
issues.impact: Mobile users cannot access the tooltip content.
issues.suggestion: Replace with a proper accessible tooltip component (e.g., Radix Tooltip) or an aria-label.

issues.title: detectWidgets uses string.includes() — may cause false positives
issues.description: `detectWidgets` uses `content.includes('<WidgetName')` which will match if the tag name appears anywhere in prose text, not just as an MDX tag.
issues.impact: Low probability but could cause unnecessary widget loading or render errors if a component name coincidentally appears in text.
issues.suggestion: Use a regex with word boundaries: `new RegExp('<${name}\\b', 'g')`

issues.title: LEA banner div has no semantic role
issues.description: The LEA orientation banner is a plain div with no `role="complementary"` or `aria-label`. It is a distinct semantic region worth marking.
issues.impact: Minor — screen reader users navigating by landmark won't see this banner as a distinct region.
issues.suggestion: Add `role="complementary"` or `aria-label="LEA test orientation"` to the banner.

issues.title: GenericBlock has no visual hint for debugging AI-hallucinated components
issues.description: GenericBlock renders children in a normal bordered box with no indication that it's a fallback for an unrecognized component name. Developers can't easily tell when content is rendering through the generic path.
issues.impact: Makes debugging harder — AI-hallucinated component names may silently render through GenericBlock without notice.
issues.suggestion: Add a subtle dotted border or a small visual indicator (e.g., a faint 'generic' label) that's visible to developers but unobtrusive to users.

issues.title: Optimistic addBookmark may silently rollback without user feedback
issues.description: The addBookmark function optimistically adds to local state then calls the server action. If the server fails, it rolls back — but the user gets no notification.
issues.impact: Users may think a bookmark was saved when it wasn't.
issues.suggestion: Add a toast notification on failed bookmark operations, similar to the existing removeBookmark rollback.
